title.zh: 卷一百二十三 列傳第七十三: 劉晏 第五琦 班宏 班紹 李巽
title.en: Volume 123 Biographies 73: Liu Yan, Di Wuqi, Ban Hong, Ban Shao, Li Xun
title.raw: 卷一百二十三 列傳第七十三: 劉晏 第五琦 班宏 班紹 李巽 Volume 123 Biographies 73: Liu Yan, Di Wuqi, Ban Hong, Ban Shao, Li Xun

sentences.zh: 劉晏，字士安，曹州南華人。

translations.literal: Liu Yan, styled Shi'an, was a man of Nanhua in Cao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yan, whose style name was Shi'an, came from Nanhua in Cao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 年七歲，舉神童，授秘書省正字。

translations.literal: At age seven he was nominated as a prodigy child and appointed Rectifier in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At the age of seven he was presented as a child prodigy and given the post of Secretariat Rectifier.

sentences.zh: 累授夏縣令，有能名。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly appointed and served as magistrate of Xia County, and had a reputation for ability.
translations.idiomatic: After successive appointments he served as magistrate of Xia County and earned a name for competence.

sentences.zh: 歷殿中侍御史，遷度支郎中、杭隴華三州刺史，尋遷河南尹。

translations.literal: He passed through the post of Attendant Censor in the Palace, was promoted to Director in the Bureau of Revenue, and became prefect of the three prefectures Hang, Long, and Hua; soon after he was transferred to Metropolitan Governor of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He served as a palace attendant censor, then was promoted to director of the revenue bureau and prefect of Hang, Long, and Hua; not long afterward he became metropolitan governor of Henan.

sentences.zh: 時史朝義盜據東都，寄理長水。

translations.literal: At that time Shi Chaoyi had seized the Eastern Capital by force, so he administered affairs from Changshui in exile.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Chaoyi had by then seized the Eastern Capital by force, so Yan governed in exile from Changshui.

sentences.zh: 入為京兆尹，頃之，加戶部侍郎、兼御史中丞，判度支，委府事於司錄張群、杜亞，綜大體，議論號為稱職。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao; before long he was additionally made Vice Minister of Revenue and concurrent Vice Censor-in-Chief, with charge over revenue affairs; he entrusted office business to the registrar Zhang Qun and Du Ya, grasped the overall situation, and his deliberations were said to be fitting to his post.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to serve as metropolitan governor of Jingzhao, and shortly thereafter was also made vice minister of revenue and concurrent vice censor-in-chief with responsibility for revenue. He left routine office work to the registrars Zhang Qun and Du Ya while he himself handled broad policy, and public opinion held that his judgment suited the office.

sentences.zh: 無何，為酷吏敬羽所構，貶通州刺史。

translations.literal: Before long he was framed by the harsh official Jing Yu and demoted to prefect of Tong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the harsh official Jing Yu framed him, and he was demoted to prefect of Tong.

sentences.zh: 復入為京兆尹、戶部侍郎，判度支。

translations.literal: He again entered the capital as Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao and Vice Minister of Revenue, with charge over revenue affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was brought back in as metropolitan governor of Jingzhao and vice minister of revenue, again overseeing revenue affairs.

sentences.zh: 時顏真卿以文學正直出為利州刺史，晏舉真卿自代為戶部，乃加國子祭酒。

translations.literal: At that time Yan Zhenqing, for his literary learning and upright character, had gone out as prefect of Li Prefecture; Yan nominated Zhenqing to replace himself in the Revenue Ministry, and Zhenqing was additionally made Rector of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zhenqing, noted for scholarship and integrity, had been sent out as prefect of Li; Yan recommended him to take over the revenue portfolio and was himself given the additional title of rector of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 寶應二年，遷吏部尚書、平章事，領度支鹽鐵轉運租庸使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Baoying he was transferred to Minister of Civil Appointments and Grand Councilor, and headed the commissioners for revenue, salt and iron, transport, and corvée-tax collection.
translations.idiomatic: In Baoying year 2 he was made minister of civil appointments and grand councilor, and took charge of revenue, salt and iron, transport, and corvée collection.

sentences.zh: 坐與中官程元振交通，元振得罪，晏罷相，為太子賓客。

translations.literal: He was implicated for associating with the eunuch Cheng Yuanzhen; when Yuanzhen fell from favor, Yan was removed as councilor and made Mentor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was punished for dealings with the eunuch Cheng Yuanzhen; when Yuanzhen fell, Yan lost his councilorship and was made mentor to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 尋授御史大夫，領東都、河南、江淮、山南等道轉運租庸鹽鐵使如故。

translations.literal: Soon after he was appointed Censor-in-Chief and, as before, headed the transport, corvée, and salt-and-iron commissioners for the Eastern Capital, Henan, Jiang-Huai, and Shannan circuits.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made censor-in-chief and continued to head transport, corvée, and salt-and-iron affairs for the Eastern Capital, Henan, Jiang-Huai, Shannan, and related circuits.

sentences.zh: 時新承兵戈之後，中外艱食，京師米價鬥至一千，官廚無兼時之積，禁軍乏食，畿縣百姓乃挼穗以供之。

translations.literal: The realm had just emerged from warfare; within and without food was scarce; in the capital the price of rice per dou reached a thousand cash; the official kitchens had no stores lasting two meals; the palace guard lacked food; and the people of the capital districts rubbed out grain ears to supply them.
translations.idiomatic: The empire had only just come through war; famine gripped court and countryside alike. In the capital a dou of rice cost a thousand cash, the palace kitchens had no reserve worth two meals, the palace armies went hungry, and people in the capital districts rubbed grain from the ears by hand to feed them.

sentences.zh: 晏受命後，以轉運為己任，凡所經歷，必究利病之由。

translations.literal: After Yan received his commission he took transport as his personal charge; everywhere he passed he invariably investigated the causes of benefit and harm.
translations.idiomatic: Once commissioned, Yan made transport his personal mission; everywhere he went he traced the roots of what helped or hurt the system.

sentences.zh: 至江淮，以書遺元載曰：

translations.literal: When he reached the Jiang-Huai region he sent a letter to Yuan Zai, saying:
translations.idiomatic: On reaching the Jiang-Huai region he wrote to Yuan Zai:

sentences.zh: 浮於淮、泗，達於汴，入於河，西循底柱、硤石、少華，楚帆越客，直抵建章、長樂，此安社稷之奇策也。

translations.literal: Floating on the Huai and Si, reaching the Bian, entering the Yellow River, proceeding west along Dizhu, Xia Rock, and Lesser Hua—Chu sails and Yue merchants straight to Jianzhang and Changle: this is the extraordinary plan to secure the altars of state.
translations.idiomatic: To float grain on the Huai and Si, reach the Bian Canal, enter the Yellow River, and follow west past Dizhu, Xia Gorge, and Lesser Hua so that Chu sails and Yue traders bear it straight to the imperial palaces—this is the bold strategy that would secure the realm.

sentences.zh: 晏賓於東朝，猶有官謗，相公終始故舊，不信流言，賈誼復召宣室，弘羊重興功利，敢不悉力以答所知。

translations.literal: Yan was a guest at the Eastern Court and still had official slander against him; the Chancellor from first to last was an old friend and did not believe floating talk—Jia Yi was again summoned to the Xuan Chamber, Sang Hongyang again raised profit and utility: how dare I not exhaust my strength to repay one who knows me?
translations.idiomatic: Though I still face official slander as a guest at the Eastern Court, you have been my friend from the beginning and will not heed rumor—like Jia Yi recalled to the Xuan Chamber or Sang Hongyang reviving state profit, I dare not hold back my full strength in repaying your trust.

sentences.zh: 驅馬陜郊，見三門渠津遺跡。

translations.literal: Driving my horse through the outskirts of Shaan, I saw the traces of the canal works at Sanmen.
translations.idiomatic: Riding through the Shaan region I saw the remains of the Sanmen canal works.

sentences.zh: 到河陰、鞏、洛，見宇文愷置梁公堰，分黃河水入通濟渠；

translations.literal: Arriving at Heyin, Gong, and Luo, I saw how Yuwen Kai had built the Liang Duke Weir to divide Yellow River water into the Tongji Canal;
translations.idiomatic: At Heyin, Gong, and Luoyang I saw Yuwen Kai's Liang Duke Weir diverting Yellow River water into the Tongji Canal;

sentences.zh: 大夫李傑新堤故事，飾像河廟，凜然如生。

translations.literal: the Grandee Li Jie's story of the new embankment, and the adorned images in the River Temple, stern as if alive.
translations.idiomatic: Grandee Li Jie's work on the new dike, and the adorned figures in the River Temple standing stern as though alive.

sentences.zh: 涉滎郊、浚澤，遙瞻淮甸，步步探討，知昔人用心，則潭、衡、桂陽必多積谷，關輔汲汲，只緣兵糧。

translations.literal: Crossing the outskirts of Xing and the dredged marshes, gazing from afar at the Huai region, step by step I investigated and knew how men of old applied their minds—then Tan, Heng, and Guiyang must have much stored grain; the Guan region is in urgent haste only because of military grain.
translations.idiomatic: Passing through the Xing outskirts and dredged marshlands and looking out toward the Huai, I examined each stretch and saw how the ancients had labored—Tan, Heng, and Guiyang must hold great grain reserves, while the capital region strains solely for lack of army rations.

sentences.zh: 漕引瀟、湘、洞庭，萬里幾日，淪波卦席，西指長安。

translations.literal: Drawing transport from the Xiao, Xiang, and Dongting, ten thousand li in how many days—billows spread like mats, pointing west to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: To channel the Xiao, Xiang, and Dongting westward—ten thousand li in a matter of days, waves spread like mats, bearing grain straight to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 三秦之人，待此而飽；

translations.literal: The people of the Three Qin wait on this to be fed;
translations.idiomatic: The people of the Three Qin would be fed by it;

sentences.zh: 六軍之眾，待此而強。

translations.literal: the hosts of the Six Armies wait on this to be strengthened.
translations.idiomatic: the Six Armies would be strengthened by it.

sentences.zh: 天子無側席之憂，都人見泛舟之役；

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven would have no worry of sitting sideways in anxiety; the people of the capital would see the work of floating boats;
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven would no longer sit uneasy on his throne, and the capital would see grain boats on the waterways;

sentences.zh: 四方旅拒者可以破膽，三河流離者於茲請命。

translations.literal: wandering resisters in the four quarters could have their courage broken; displaced people of the Three Rivers would here plead for their lives.
translations.idiomatic: rebels in distant regions would lose heart, and refugees of the Three Rivers would here beg for relief.

sentences.zh: 相公匡戴明主，為富人侯，此今之切務，不可失也。

translations.literal: The Chancellor supports and bears up a brilliant lord, becoming a rich man's marquis—this is the urgent task of today and must not be missed.
translations.idiomatic: You who support a brilliant sovereign and may become a lord of wealth—this is the urgent task of our age and must not be let slip.

sentences.zh: 使仆湔洗瑕穢，率罄愚懦，當憑經義，請護河堤，冥勤在官，不辭水死。

translations.literal: Let your servant wash away stains, leading forth all my foolish timidity; I shall rely on canonical principles, request to guard the river dikes, labor in office in obscurity, and not refuse death by water.
translations.idiomatic: Let me wash away my faults and offer all my feeble wit; guided by principle I ask to guard the river dikes, labor in office without complaint, and face drowning if need be.

sentences.zh: 然運之利病，各有四五焉。

translations.literal: Yet the benefits and harms of transport each have four or five points.
translations.idiomatic: Yet transport has its gains and its troubles, four or five of each.

sentences.zh: 晏自尹京入為計相，共五年矣。

translations.literal: Yan, from governing Jingzhao to entering office as finance chancellor, has altogether been five years.
translations.idiomatic: From my years governing Jingzhao to serving as finance chancellor, it has been five years in all.

sentences.zh: 京師三輔百姓，唯苦稅畝傷多，若使江、湖米來每年三二十萬，即頓減徭賦，歌舞皇澤，其利一也。

translations.literal: The people of the capital and the Three Adjuncts suffer only from heavy land-tax assessments; if rice from the rivers and lakes came two or three hundred thousand [shi] each year, corvée and levies would at once be reduced and they would sing and dance under the imperial grace—this is the first benefit.
translations.idiomatic: The people of the capital districts suffer chiefly from crushing land taxes; if two or three hundred thousand shi of grain came yearly from the rivers and lakes, levies would drop at once and they would rejoice in the emperor's bounty—the first benefit.

sentences.zh: 東都殘毀，百無一存。

translations.literal: The Eastern Capital lies in ruins; not one in a hundred remains.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Capital lies in ruins; scarcely one building in a hundred still stands.

sentences.zh: 若米運流通，則饑人皆附，村落邑厘，從此滋多。

translations.literal: If grain transport flowed freely, the hungry would all attach themselves; villages and hamlets would from this multiply.
translations.idiomatic: If grain transport were restored, the hungry would gather there and villages and market towns would spring up again.

sentences.zh: 受命之日引海陵之倉以食鞏、洛，是計之得者，其利二也。

translations.literal: From the day of receiving the commission, to draw on Hailing's granaries to feed Gong and Luo is a plan that succeeds—this is the second benefit.
translations.idiomatic: From the day I took office I could draw on Hailing's granaries to feed Gong and Luoyang—a sound plan and the second benefit.

sentences.zh: 諸將有在邊者，諸戎有侵敗王略者，或聞三江、五湖，貢輸紅粒，雲帆桂楫，輸納帝鄉，軍誌曰：「先聲後實，可以震耀夷夏。

translations.literal: Generals stationed on the frontier, barbarians who invade and defeat the royal domain—if they heard that from the Three Rivers and Five Lakes tribute of red grain was sent, cloud sails and cassia oars bearing it to the imperial homeland, the military maxim says: 'First sound, then substance—this can awe barbarians and Chinese alike.'
translations.idiomatic: For generals on the frontier and for barbarians who encroach on the realm, to hear that red grain from the Three Rivers and Five Lakes sails on cloud-white banners and cassia-wood oars to the imperial capital would fulfill the maxim that reputation precedes force and can overawe both Chinese and foreigners alike.

sentences.zh: 」其利三也。

translations.literal: ' This is the third benefit.
translations.idiomatic: That would be the third benefit.

sentences.zh: 自古帝王之盛，皆云書同文，車同軌，日月所照，莫不率俾。

translations.literal: From antiquity the splendor of emperors and kings has been said to be uniform script and uniform wheel-tracks; wherever sun and moon shine, none fail to follow and serve.
translations.idiomatic: Since antiquity the glory of sage rulers has been told as one script and one gauge for wheels, with all beneath the sun and moon submitting in turn.

sentences.zh: 今舟車既通，商賈往來，百貨雜集，航海梯山，聖神輝光，漸近貞觀、永徽之盛，其利四也。

translations.literal: Now that boats and carts are connected, merchants come and go, all goods gather in mixture, sailing the sea and scaling mountains—the sage spirit's radiance gradually approaches the splendor of Zhenguan and Yonghui: this is the fourth benefit.
translations.idiomatic: With waterways and roads linked again, merchants would travel, goods would gather from sea and mountain, and the sage radiance of the throne would draw near the prosperity of the Zhenguan and Yonghui eras—the fourth benefit.

sentences.zh: 所可疑者，函、陜雕殘，東周尤甚。

translations.literal: What gives cause for doubt is that Hangu and Shaan are carved to ruin, and Eastern Zhou especially so.
translations.idiomatic: What gives pause is that the Hangu and Shaan region lies in ruins, Eastern Zhou worst of all.

sentences.zh: 過宜陽、熊耳，至武牢、成臯，五百里中，編戶千余而已。

translations.literal: Passing Yiyang and Xiong'er, reaching Wulao and Chenggao, within five hundred li there are only a little over a thousand registered households.
translations.idiomatic: From Yiyang and Xiong'er to Wulao and Chenggao, five hundred li hold barely a thousand registered households.

sentences.zh: 居無尺椽，人無煙爨，蕭條淒慘，獸遊鬼哭。

translations.literal: Dwellings lack a foot of rafter; people lack cooking smoke; desolate and wretched, beasts roam and ghosts weep.
translations.idiomatic: Homes lack even a foot of timber, hearths show no smoke, and desolation is so deep that beasts wander the roads and ghosts seem to wail.

sentences.zh: 牛必羸角，輿必說輹，棧車輓漕，亦不易求。

translations.literal: Oxen must be withered at the horns; carts must have their wheel-hubs removed; plank carts for hauling transport are also not easily found.
translations.idiomatic: Oxen are wasted to the horn, cart hubs are stripped away, and even plank carts for haulage are hard to find.

sentences.zh: 今於無人之境，興此勞人之運，固難就矣，其病一也。

translations.literal: Now to raise this labor-consuming transport in a land without people is inherently hard to accomplish—this is the first harm.
translations.idiomatic: To launch this labor-heavy transport through uninhabited country is bound to fail—that is the first difficulty.

sentences.zh: 河、汴有初，不修則毀澱，故每年正月發近縣丁男，塞長茭，決沮淤，清明桃花已後，遠水自然安流，陽侯、宓妃，不復太息。

translations.literal: The Yellow River and Bian Canal had their origins; if not maintained they are destroyed by silt, so every year in the first month men from nearby counties are mobilized to block long rushes, open clogged mud, and after Clear Brightness and the peach blossoms distant waters naturally flow in peace—Lord Yang and Lady Mi no longer sigh deeply.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow River and Bian Canal must be dredged yearly or silt destroys them; each first month laborers from nearby counties block rushes and clear mud, and after Clear Brightness the distant currents run calm again—the river spirits need sigh no more.

sentences.zh: 頃因寇難，總不掏拓，澤滅水，岸石崩，役夫需於沙，津吏旋於濘，千里洄上，罔水舟行，其病二也。

translations.literal: Recently because of bandit troubles dredging has altogether ceased; marshes swallow the water, bank stones collapse, laborers wait on sand, ferry clerks turn in mud, for a thousand li upstream there is no water for boats to travel—this is the second harm.
translations.idiomatic: Lately, because of rebellion, dredging has stopped altogether; marshes have swallowed the channel, banks have collapsed, laborers stand idle on sandbars, ferry officials spin in mud, and for a thousand li upstream there is no depth for boats—the second difficulty.

sentences.zh: 東垣、底柱，澠池、二陵，北河運處五六百里，戍卒久絕，縣吏空拳。

translations.literal: From Eastern Yuan and Dizhu through Mianchi and the Two Mounds, along five or six hundred li of the northern river transport route, garrison soldiers have long been cut off and county clerks have empty fists.
translations.idiomatic: From Eastern Yuan and Dizhu through Mianchi and the Two Mounds, five or six hundred li of the northern transport route have no garrison troops left and county officials have no force at hand.

sentences.zh: 奪攘奸宄，窟穴囊橐。

translations.literal: Robbery and plunder by villains; dens and pouches of booty.
translations.idiomatic: Robbers and traitors seize goods and hole up with their plunder.

sentences.zh: 夾河為藪，豺狼狺狺，舟行所經，寇亦能往，其病三也。

translations.literal: Along the river are marshes; wolves and jackals snarl; wherever boats pass, bandits can also go—this is the third harm.
translations.idiomatic: Marshes line the riverbanks, wolves snarl along the route, and wherever boats can go bandits can go too—the third difficulty.

sentences.zh: 東自淮陰，西臨蒲阪，亙三千里，屯戍相望。

translations.literal: From Huaiyin in the east to Pufan in the west, spanning three thousand li, garrison posts face one another.
translations.idiomatic: From Huaiyin in the east to Pufan in the west, three thousand li of garrison posts stand face to face.

sentences.zh: 中軍皆鼎司元侯，賤卒儀同青紫，每雲食半菽，又雲無挾纊，輓漕所至，船到便留，即非單車使折簡書所能制矣，其病四也。

translations.literal: Central armies are all chief ministers and great marquises; lowly soldiers are the equal of purple and scarlet rank; they always say they eat half beans, and again say they have no cotton quilt; wherever hauling transport arrives, when the boat comes they detain it—this is not something a lone envoy with a folded letter can control: this is the fourth harm.
translations.idiomatic: The central armies are filled with chief ministers and great lords, while common soldiers dress like officials of high rank; they claim half a meal of beans and no quilt for warmth, yet wherever transport boats arrive they are held up on the spot—not something a lone commissioner with a letter can restrain—the fourth difficulty.

sentences.zh: 惟小子畢其慮奔走之，惟中書詳其利病裁成之。

translations.literal: Only your humble servant will exhaust his plans and run about it; only the Secretariat will examine its benefits and harms and cut and complete it.
translations.idiomatic: Only I will exhaust my wits in carrying it out; only the Secretariat can weigh its gains and losses and bring it to completion.

sentences.zh: 晏累年已來，事缺名毀，聖慈含育，特賜生全。

translations.literal: Yan for many years has had affairs lacking and name destroyed; the sage compassion nurtured him and specially granted him life intact.
translations.idiomatic: For years my record has been flawed and my name tarnished, yet imperial mercy spared my life.

sentences.zh: 月余家居，遽即臨遣，恩榮感切，思殞百身。

translations.literal: A little over a month at home in retirement, then suddenly summoned and dispatched—the grace and glory moved him deeply; he thought to die a hundred deaths.
translations.idiomatic: After little more than a month at home I was suddenly sent out on mission; the grace overwhelmed me and I would have given a hundred lives in return.

sentences.zh: 見一水不通，願荷鍤而先往；

translations.literal: Seeing one waterway not connected, he wished to shoulder the spade and go first;
translations.idiomatic: Where a channel was blocked I wished to take up the spade and go first;

sentences.zh: 見一粒不運，願負米而先趨。

translations.literal: seeing one grain not transported, he wished to carry rice on his back and hurry ahead.
translations.idiomatic: where a single grain failed to move I wished to carry rice on my back and run ahead.

sentences.zh: 焦心苦形，期報明主，丹誠未克，漕引多虞，屏營中流，掩泣獻狀。

translations.literal: He scorched his heart and wore his body down, hoping to repay the brilliant lord; red sincerity had not yet succeeded, transport drawing had many anxieties; he paced in distress midstream and, covering his tears, presented this memorial.
translations.idiomatic: I wore myself thin with worry, hoping to repay my sovereign; though my loyalty was not yet fulfilled and transport still faced many doubts, I paced the river in distress and, weeping, submitted this report.

sentences.zh: 自此每歲運米數十萬石以濟關中。

translations.literal: From this time each year several hundred thousand shi of rice were transported to relieve Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: From then on several hundred thousand shi of rice were shipped each year to supply Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 又至德初，為國用不足，令第五琦於諸道榷鹽以助軍用，及晏代其任，法益精密，官無遺利。

translations.literal: Moreover, at the beginning of Zhide, because state expenditures were insufficient, Di Wuqi was ordered to monopolize salt in the various circuits to aid military use; when Yan replaced him in the post, the law grew more precise and detailed, and the government left no profit uncollected.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhide era, with state funds short, Di Wuqi was ordered to impose salt monopolies across the circuits to support the armies; when Yan took over, the system grew tighter still and the government left no revenue on the table.

sentences.zh: 初，歲入錢六十萬貫，季年所入逾十倍，而人無厭苦。

translations.literal: At first yearly intake was six hundred thousand strings of cash; in the final years intake exceeded tenfold, yet the people had no weariness or suffering.
translations.idiomatic: At first annual receipts were six hundred thousand strings of cash; in later years they rose more than tenfold, yet the people did not complain.

sentences.zh: 大歷末，通計一歲征賦所入總一千二百萬貫，而鹽利且過半。

translations.literal: At the end of Dali, reckoning all levies and taxes for one year, the total intake was twelve million strings of cash, and salt profits alone exceeded half.
translations.idiomatic: By the end of the Dali era total annual tax receipts reached twelve million strings of cash, with salt profits alone accounting for more than half.

sentences.zh: 累遷吏部尚書。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Minister of Civil Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive promotions to minister of civil appointments.

sentences.zh: 大歷四年六月，與右僕射裴遵慶同赴本曹視事，敕尚食增置儲供，許內侍魚朝恩及宰臣已下常朝官鹹詣省送上。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fourth year of Dali, together with Right Vice Director Pei Zunqing he went to his department to oversee affairs; an edict ordered the Imperial Commissary to increase stored provisions, permitting the eunuch Yu Chao'en and all regular court officials down to the grand councilors to go to the ministry and present gifts.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Dali year 4 he and right vice director Pei Zunqing went together to oversee their ministry; the emperor ordered extra provisions from the imperial kitchen and allowed the eunuch Yu Chao'en and all regular court officials down to the grand councilors to visit the ministry with congratulatory gifts.

sentences.zh: 八年，知三銓選事。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he took charge of selection affairs in the Three Bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: In year 8 he took charge of selection affairs in all three appointment bureaus.

sentences.zh: 十二年三月，誅宰臣元載，晏奉詔訊鞫。

translations.literal: In the third month of the twelfth year the grand councilor Yuan Zai was executed; Yan received an edict to interrogate and examine.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of year 12 the grand councilor Yuan Zai was put to death, and Yan was ordered to conduct the interrogation.

sentences.zh: 晏以載居任樹黨，布於天下，不敢專斷，請他官共事。

translations.literal: Yan, because Zai in office had planted factions spread through the realm, did not dare decide alone and requested other officials to share the work.
translations.idiomatic: Because Zai had built a factional network across the empire while in office, Yan did not dare rule alone and asked other officials to join the inquiry.

sentences.zh: 敕御史大夫李涵、右散騎常侍蕭昕、兵部侍郎袁傪、禮部侍郎常袞、諫議大夫杜亞同推，載皆款伏。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Censor-in-Chief Li Han, Right Regular Attendant Xiao Xin, Vice Minister of War Yuan Kan, Vice Minister of Rites Chang Gao, and Remonstrance Grandee Du Ya to investigate together; Zai fully confessed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Censor-in-Chief Li Han, Right Regular Attendant Xiao Xin, Vice Minister of War Yuan Kan, Vice Minister of Rites Chang Gao, and Remonstrance Grandee Du Ya to join the inquiry; Zai confessed to everything.

sentences.zh: 初，晏承旨，門下侍郎、同平章事王縉亦處極法，晏謂涵等曰：重刑再覆，國之常典，況誅大臣，得不覆奏？

translations.literal: Initially, when Yan received the imperial order, Wang Jin, Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate Grand Councilor, was also to receive the extreme penalty; Yan said to Han and the others: 'When a heavy sentence is imposed, a second review is the state's regular rule; moreover, when executing a great minister, must one not submit a second memorial for review?'
translations.idiomatic: When Yan first received the order, Wang Jin, vice director of the secretariat and associate grand councilor, was also slated for the death penalty. Yan told Han and the others: 'A second review of a heavy sentence is standard state practice; when a great minister is to be executed, must we not submit a follow-up memorial?'

sentences.zh: 又法有首從，二人同刑，亦宜重取進止。

translations.literal: Moreover the law distinguishes principal and follower; when two men share the same penalty, one should again seek the sovereign's decision.
translations.idiomatic: The law also distinguishes ringleader from follower; when two men face the same penalty, we should again seek the throne's final decision.

sentences.zh: 」涵等從命。

translations.literal: ' Han and the others obeyed the order.
translations.idiomatic: Han and the others complied.

sentences.zh: 及晏等覆奏，代宗乃減縉罪從輕。

translations.literal: When Yan and the others submitted the follow-up memorial, Daizong then reduced Jin's crime to a lighter penalty.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan and the others submitted their follow-up memorial, Daizong lightened Jin's sentence.

sentences.zh: 縉之生，晏平反之力也。

translations.literal: Jin's living was due to Yan's power to reverse the verdict.
translations.idiomatic: Jin owed his life to Yan's intervention.

sentences.zh: 十三年十二月，為尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the thirteenth year he became Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of year 13 he was made left vice director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 時宰臣常袞專政，以晏久掌銓衡，時議平允，兼司儲蓄，職舉功深，慮公望日崇，上心有屬。

translations.literal: At that time the grand councilor Chang Gao monopolized government; because Yan had long held the scales of selection, public opinion held him fair, and he also managed storage—his duties were fulfilled and his achievements deep—they feared his public standing daily rose and the sovereign's heart had someone in mind.
translations.idiomatic: Grand councilor Chang Gao then dominated the government. Yan had long controlled appointments and was regarded as even-handed, while also managing state stores with deep achievement; Chang feared Yan's public standing was rising daily and that the emperor's favor might turn toward him.

sentences.zh: 竊忌之，乃奏晏朝廷舊德，宜為百吏師長，外示崇重，內實去其權。

translations.literal: Secretly jealous, he memorialized that Yan was an old virtue of the court and ought to be teacher and leader of the hundred officials—outwardly showing honor and weight, inwardly in fact removing his power.
translations.idiomatic: Jealous in private, he memorialized that Yan, a veteran of the court, should become mentor to the officials—honoring him in name while stripping his real authority.

sentences.zh: 及奏上，以晏使務方理，代其任者難其人，使務、知三銓並如故。

translations.literal: When the memorial went up, because Yan's commissioner duties were being put in order and a replacement was hard to find, his commissioner duties and charge over the Three Bureaus selections remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial reached the throne, Yan's transport duties were still in good order and no suitable replacement could be found, so his transport portfolio and control of the three selection bureaus remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 李靈曜之亂也，河南節帥所據，多不奉法令，征賦亦隨之；

translations.literal: In the rebellion of Li Lingyao, the territories held by the Henan military commissioners for the most part did not obey laws and edicts, and tax levies followed suit;
translations.idiomatic: During Li Lingyao's rebellion the Henan military commissioners for the most part ignored imperial law, and tax collection suffered accordingly;

sentences.zh: 州縣雖益減，晏以羨余相補，人不加賦，所入仍舊，議者稱其能。

translations.literal: though prefectures and counties had further reductions, Yan used surplus to compensate; the people were not given added levies, and intake remained as before—commentators praised his ability.
translations.idiomatic: though prefectures and counties reported further shortfalls, Yan used surpluses elsewhere to cover them so the people faced no new levies and revenue held steady—observers praised his skill.

sentences.zh: 自諸道巡院距京師，重價募疾足，置遞相望，四方物價之上下，雖極遠不四五日知，故食貨之重輕，盡權在掌握，朝廷獲美利而天下無甚貴甚賤之憂，得其術矣。

translations.literal: From the circuit inspection offices to the capital he paid high prices to recruit swift runners and set relay posts facing one another; the rise and fall of prices in the four quarters, though extremely distant, were known within four or five days—thus the weight and lightness of food and goods lay wholly in his grasp; the court obtained fine profit and the realm had no worry of extreme dearth or extreme cheapness: he had got the method.
translations.idiomatic: From his circuit inspection offices to the capital he hired swift couriers at high pay and set relay posts along the routes, so price movements even in the farthest regions were known within four or five days. He thus controlled the weight of goods and money, brought handsome profit to the court, and kept the realm from extreme inflation or collapse—he had mastered the art.

sentences.zh: 凡所任使，多收後進有幹能者。

translations.literal: In all those he appointed and used, he mostly recruited younger men of ability and practical talent.
translations.idiomatic: In appointments he favored promising younger men of proven ability.

sentences.zh: 其所總領，務乎急促，趨利者化之，遂以成風。

translations.literal: What he headed overall was bent on urgency and haste; those who chased profit were transformed by him, and thus it became a prevailing custom.
translations.idiomatic: The offices he led prized speed above all, and those who sought profit followed his example until haste became the norm.

sentences.zh: 當時權勢，或以親戚為托，晏亦應之，俸給之多少，命官之遲速，必如其誌，然未嘗得親職事。

translations.literal: Men of power at the time sometimes entrusted relatives to him; Yan also responded—the amount of salary stipend, the speed of appointment orders, always matched their wishes, yet they never obtained substantive duties in person.
translations.idiomatic: Powerful men often asked him to place their relatives; Yan obliged on salary and the timing of appointments, yet never gave them substantive posts.

sentences.zh: 其所領要務，必一時之選，故晏沒後二十余年，韓洄、元琇、裴腆、包佶、盧征、李衡繼掌財賦，皆晏故吏。

translations.literal: The important duties he headed were always men chosen for the moment; thus more than twenty years after Yan's death Han Hui, Yuan Xiu, Pei Tian, Bao Ji, Lu Zheng, and Li Heng in succession held finance and tax affairs—all were Yan's former clerks.
translations.idiomatic: For key posts he chose the best men of the day, so more than twenty years after his death Han Hui, Yuan Xiu, Pei Tian, Bao Ji, Lu Zheng, and Li Heng in turn ran state finance—all former subordinates of his.

sentences.zh: 其部吏居數千里之外，奉教令如在目前，雖寢興宴語，而無欺紿，四方動靜，莫不先知，事有可賀者，必先上章奏。

translations.literal: His subordinate clerks dwelt several thousand li away yet carried out his orders as if he were before their eyes; though at rest or rising, at feast or talk, there was no deception—all movements in the four quarters he knew beforehand, and when something was worth congratulation they first submitted a memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Subordinates thousands of li away obeyed his orders as if he stood before them; whether waking or sleeping, at feast or in talk, none deceived him. He learned of events across the realm before anyone else, and good news was reported to him by memorial before all others.

sentences.zh: 江淮茶、橘，晏與本道觀察使各歲貢之，皆欲其先至。

translations.literal: Tea and oranges of the Jiang-Huai—Yan and each circuit observation commissioner yearly presented them as tribute, each wanting theirs to arrive first.
translations.idiomatic: Tea and oranges from the Jiang-Huai were presented yearly as tribute by Yan and each circuit observation commissioner, each striving to arrive first.

sentences.zh: 有土之官，或封山斷道，禁前發者，晏厚以財力致之，常先他司，由是甚不為籓鎮所便。

translations.literal: Local officials sometimes sealed mountains and cut roads, forbidding early dispatch; Yan used heavy wealth to obtain them and usually arrived before other offices—therefore he was greatly disliked by the military commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: Local officials sometimes blocked roads to keep tribute from leaving early; Yan spent heavily to secure priority and usually beat other offices—making him deeply unpopular with the regional commanders.

sentences.zh: 晏理家以儉約稱，而重交敦舊，頗以財貨遺天下名土，故人多稱之。

translations.literal: Yan managed his household with a reputation for frugality, yet valued friendship and honored old ties, and quite often bestowed goods and wealth on famous scholars of the realm—therefore many praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Yan ran his household frugally, yet cherished old friendships and often gave money to renowned scholars across the land, which won him wide praise.

sentences.zh: 善訓諸子，鹹有學藝。

translations.literal: He was skilled in instructing his sons; all had learning and arts.
translations.idiomatic: He trained his sons well, and all gained learning and skill.

sentences.zh: 任事十余年，權勢之重，鄰於宰相，要官重職，頗出其門。

translations.literal: In office more than ten years, the weight of his power bordered on that of a chancellor; important offices and heavy posts largely came from his gate.
translations.idiomatic: After more than ten years in power his authority rivaled that of a chancellor, and many key offices passed through his followers.

sentences.zh: 既有材力，視事敏速，乘機無滯，然多任數，挾權貴，固恩澤，有口者必利啖之。

translations.literal: He had both talent and strength, handled affairs swiftly and sensitively, seized opportunity without delay—yet he often relied on calculation, leveraged the powerful and noble, secured favor and grace, and anyone with a mouth he surely fed with profit.
translations.idiomatic: Talented and decisive, he handled business with speed and seized every opening—yet he relied heavily on maneuver, cultivated the powerful, secured imperial favor, and bought off anyone who might speak against him.

sentences.zh: 當大歷時，事貴因循，軍國之用，皆仰於晏，未嘗檢轄。

translations.literal: During the Dali era affairs prized following precedent; military and state expenditures all depended on Yan, and were never inspected or controlled.
translations.idiomatic: In the Dali era government prized routine; military and civil spending all depended on Yan and went largely unchecked.

sentences.zh: 德宗嗣位，言事者稱轉運可罷多矣。

translations.literal: When Dezong succeeded to the throne, memorialists said many times that transport could be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: When Dezong came to the throne, many memorialists argued that the transport system should be abolished.

sentences.zh: 初，楊炎為吏部侍郎，晏為尚書，各恃權使氣，兩不相得。

translations.literal: Earlier, Yang Yan was Vice Minister of Civil Appointments and Yan was Minister; each relied on power and vented his temper—the two did not get along.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Yang Yan was vice minister of civil appointments and Yan was minister, each abused his authority and the two could not abide each other.

sentences.zh: 炎坐元載貶，晏快之，昌言於朝。

translations.literal: Yan was demoted because of Yuan Zai; Yan rejoiced at this and spoke openly at court.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Yan was demoted because of Yuan Zai, Yan rejoiced and spoke openly against him at court.

sentences.zh: 及炎入相，追怒前事，且以晏與元載隙憾，時人言載之得罪，晏有力焉。

translations.literal: When Yan entered office as chancellor he pursued his anger over past matters, and moreover because Yan and Yuan Zai had a rift and grudge—people of the time said that in Zai's falling from grace Yan had exerted force.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Yan became chancellor he nursed that grudge and noted Yan's feud with Yuan Zai; contemporaries said Yan had helped bring Zai down.

sentences.zh: 炎將為載復仇，又時人風言代宗寵獨孤妃而又愛其子韓王迥，晏密啟請立獨孤為皇后。

translations.literal: Yan was about to avenge Zai, and moreover people at the time whispered that Daizong favored Consort Dugu and also loved her son, Prince Han Huai; Yan had secretly memorialized asking to establish Dugu as empress.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yan meant to avenge Zai, and rumor held that Daizong favored Consort Dugu and her son Prince Han of Huai; Yan had secretly urged making Dugu empress.

sentences.zh: 炎因對易攵流涕奏言：「賴祖宗福祐，先皇與陛下不為賊臣所間。

translations.literal: Yan thereupon addressed the throne in tears, memorializing: 'Thanks to the blessings of the ancestors, the late emperor and Your Majesty were not set apart by treacherous ministers.'
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yan then addressed the throne in tears: 'By the blessings of our ancestors, the late emperor and Your Majesty were not torn apart by traitorous ministers.'

sentences.zh: 不然，劉晏、黎幹之輩，搖動社稷，兇謀果矣。

translations.literal: Otherwise, men like Liu Yan and Li Gan would have shaken the altars of state, and the wicked plot would have succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise men like Liu Yan and Li Gan would have shaken the throne, and their wicked plot would have succeeded.

sentences.zh: 今幹以伏罪，晏猶領權，臣為宰相，不能正持此事，罪當萬死。

translations.literal: Now Gan has submitted to punishment, yet Yan still holds power; your servant as chancellor cannot set this matter straight—his crime deserves ten thousand deaths.'
translations.idiomatic: Gan has now paid for his crime, yet Yan still holds power; as chancellor I have failed to correct this and deserve death ten thousand times over.'

sentences.zh: 」崔祐甫奏言：「此事曖昧，陛下以廓然大赦，不當究尋虛語。

translations.literal: ' Cui Youfu memorialized: 'This matter is obscure; Your Majesty, with your broad amnesty, ought not pursue empty talk.'
translations.idiomatic: Cui Youfu replied: 'This matter is unclear; Your Majesty has proclaimed a great amnesty and should not pursue idle rumor.'

sentences.zh: 」硃泚、崔寧又從傍與祐甫救解之，寧言頗切，炎大怒，故斥寧令出鎮鄜坊以摧挫之。

translations.literal: ' Zhu Ci and Cui Ning also from the side joined Youfu in pleading for resolution; Ning's words were quite sharp—Yan was greatly angered and therefore expelled Ning, ordering him out to govern Zuo-Fang to break and humiliate him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ci and Cui Ning sided with Youfu in mediation; Ning spoke sharply, and Yang Yan in fury sent him out to govern Zuo-Fang as punishment.

sentences.zh: 遂罷晏轉運等使，尋貶為忠州刺史。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yan's transport and other commissioner posts were abolished, and soon after he was demoted to prefect of Zhong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's transport commissions were abolished, and he was soon demoted to prefect of Zhong.

sentences.zh: 炎欲誣構其罪，知庾準與晏素有隙，舉為荊南節度，以伺晏動靜。

translations.literal: Yan wished to fabricate crimes against him; knowing that Yu Zhun and Yan had long had a rift, he recommended Zhun as military commissioner of Jingnan to watch Yan's movements.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yan sought to frame him and, knowing Yu Zhun's old enmity with Yan, had Zhun appointed Jingnan commissioner to spy on him.

sentences.zh: 準乃奏晏與硃泚書祈救解，言多怨望，炎又證成其事，上以為然。

translations.literal: Zhun then memorialized that Yan in letters to Zhu Ci had begged for rescue and release, with many words of resentment; Yan also corroborated the matter, and the emperor believed it true.
translations.idiomatic: Zhun memorialized that Yan had written Zhu Ci begging release with bitter complaints; Yang Yan corroborated the charge, and the emperor believed it.

sentences.zh: 是月庚午，晏已受誅，使回奏報，誣晏以忠州謀叛，下詔暴言其罪，時年六十六，天下冤之。

translations.literal: That month on the gengwu day Yan had already been executed; when the envoy returned to report, he slandered Yan as plotting rebellion at Zhong Prefecture; an edict publicly proclaimed his crimes; he was sixty-six years old, and the realm considered it an injustice.
translations.idiomatic: That month on the day gengwu Yan had already been executed; the returning envoy falsely reported a plot to rebel from Zhong, and an edict publicly listed his crimes. He was sixty-six, and the empire regarded his death as a grievous wrong.

sentences.zh: 家屬徙嶺表，連累者數十人。

translations.literal: His family was banished to the Lingnan region, and several tens were implicated with him.
translations.idiomatic: His family was exiled to the far south, and dozens of others were implicated.

sentences.zh: 貞元五年，上悟，方錄晏子執經，授太常博士；

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhenyuan the emperor came to his senses and then enrolled Yan's son Zhijing, appointing him Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices;
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyuan year 5 the emperor saw his error and enrolled Yan's son Zhijing as an erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices;

sentences.zh: 少子宗經，秘書郎。

translations.literal: his younger son Zongjing became a Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: his younger son Zongjing became a secretary.

sentences.zh: 執經上請削官贈父，特追贈鄭州刺史。

translations.literal: Zhijing memorialized asking to strip his own office to posthumously honor his father, and Yan was specially posthumously enfeoffed as prefect of Zheng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhijing asked to surrender his own rank to honor his father posthumously, and Yan was specially posthumously made prefect of Zheng.

sentences.zh: 第五琦，京兆長安人。

translations.literal: Di Wuqi was a man of Chang'an in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Di Wuqi came from Chang'an in the capital district.

sentences.zh: 少孤，事兄華，敬順過人。

translations.literal: Orphaned young, he served his elder brother Hua with respect and deference surpassing others.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned in youth, he served his elder brother Hua with exceptional respect and obedience.

sentences.zh: 及長，有吏才，以富國強兵之術自任。

translations.literal: When grown he had talent for administration and took upon himself methods to enrich the state and strengthen the army.
translations.idiomatic: As an adult he showed administrative talent and devoted himself to policies to enrich the state and strengthen the armies.

sentences.zh: 天寶初，事韋堅，堅敗貶官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao he served Wei Jian; when Jian failed he was demoted in office.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianbao era he served under Wei Jian and was demoted when Jian fell.

sentences.zh: 累至須江丞，時太守賀蘭進明甚重之。

translations.literal: He rose through posts to assistant magistrate of Xujiang; at the time the prefect Helan Jinming greatly valued him.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to assistant magistrate of Xujiang, where Prefect Helan Jinming held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 會安祿山反，進明遷北海郡太守，奏琦為錄事參軍。

translations.literal: When An Lushan rebelled, Jinming was transferred to prefect of Beihai Commandery and memorialized Qi as recording secretary and military adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan rebelled, Jinming became prefect of Beihai and recommended Qi as his recording secretary.

sentences.zh: 祿山已陷河間、信都等五郡，進明未有戰功，玄宗大怒，遣中使封刀促之，曰：「收地不得，即斬進明之首。

translations.literal: Lushan had already taken Hejian, Xindu, and five other commanderies; Jinming had no military achievement; Xuanzong was greatly angered and sent a palace envoy with a sealed sword to urge him, saying: 'If you do not recover the territory, then cut off Jinming's head.'
translations.idiomatic: Lushan had seized Hejian, Xindu, and five other commanderies while Jinming had won no victory. Xuanzong in fury sent a palace envoy bearing a sealed sword with the order: 'Recover the lost territory or take Jinming's head.'

sentences.zh: 」進明惶懼，莫知所出，琦乃勸令厚以財帛募勇敢士，出奇力戰，遂收所陷之郡。

translations.literal: ' Jinming was fearful and knew not what to do; Qi then urged him to use generous wealth and silks to recruit brave men, strike with unexpected force, and thus recover the commanderies that had fallen.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Jinming knew not what to do. Qi urged him to spend heavily recruiting brave men, strike with surprise, and recover the lost commanderies.

sentences.zh: 令琦奏事，至蜀中，琦得謁見，奏言：「方今之急在兵，兵之強弱在賦，賦之所出，江淮居多。

translations.literal: He had Qi present a memorial; reaching Shu, Qi obtained an audience and memorialized: 'The present urgency lies in the army; the army's strength or weakness lies in levies; where levies come from, the Jiang-Huai region supplies the greater part.'
translations.idiomatic: Qi was sent to report to court; reaching Shu he gained audience and said: 'The urgent need is armies, armies depend on revenue, and most revenue comes from the Jiang-Huai.'

sentences.zh: 若假臣職任，使濟軍須，臣能使賞給之資，不勞聖慮。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty grants me office and charge to supply the army's needs, your servant can provide funds for rewards and disbursements without troubling the sage mind.'
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty grants me authority to supply the armies, I can provide funds for pay and rewards without burdening the throne.'

sentences.zh: 」玄宗大喜，即日拜監察御史，勾當江淮租庸使。

translations.literal: ' Xuanzong was greatly pleased and that same day appointed him Investigating Censor, with charge as Jiang-Huai corvée-tax commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong was delighted and that same day made him investigating censor in charge of Jiang-Huai corvée and tax collection.

sentences.zh: 尋拜殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: Soon after he was appointed Attendant Censor in the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made a palace attendant censor.

sentences.zh: 尋加山南等五道度支使，促辦應卒，事無違闕。

translations.literal: Soon after he was additionally made revenue commissioner for Shannan and four other circuits, pressing completion to meet emergencies; in affairs there was no shortfall.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon also made revenue commissioner for Shannan and four other circuits, meeting every emergency without fail.

sentences.zh: 遷司金郎中、兼御史中丞，使如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director in the Bureau of Coinage, concurrent Vice Censor-in-Chief, with his commissioner duties as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to director of the coinage bureau and concurrent vice censor-in-chief, retaining his commissioner posts.

sentences.zh: 於是創立鹽法，就山海井竈收榷其鹽，官置吏出糶。

translations.literal: Thereupon he established the salt law, collecting monopoly tax on salt from mountains, seas, wells, and hearths, with officials appointed to sell it out.
translations.idiomatic: He then created the salt monopoly, taxing production at mountains, seas, wells, and salt works and selling through government agents.

sentences.zh: 其舊業戶並浮人願為業者，免其雜徭，隸鹽鐵使，盜煮私市罪有差。

translations.literal: Former producers and floating persons who wished to enter the trade were exempted from miscellaneous corvées, placed under the salt-and-iron commissioner, and crimes of illicit boiling and private sale were graded in severity.
translations.idiomatic: Established producers and newcomers were freed from miscellaneous corvées, placed under the salt commissioner, and penalties for illegal production and sale were graded by severity.

sentences.zh: 百姓除租庸外，無得橫賦，人不益稅而上用以饒。

translations.literal: The common people, apart from corvée and land tax, had no arbitrary levies imposed; the people were not given added taxes yet state use was ample.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond regular corvée and land tax the people faced no arbitrary levies; taxes did not rise yet state revenue grew ample.

sentences.zh: 遷戶部侍郎、兼御史丞，專判度支，領河南等道支度都勾當轉運租庸鹽鐵鑄錢、司農太府出納、山南東西江西淮南館驛等使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Revenue and concurrent Vice Censor, with sole charge over revenue affairs, heading the commissioners for disbursement, transport, corvée, salt and iron, coinage, intake and outlay of the Court of the Imperial Granary and Grand Storehouse, and postal stations of Henan, eastern and western Shannan, Jiangxi, Huainan, and other circuits.
translations.idiomatic: He became vice minister of revenue and concurrent vice censor with sole charge of revenue, heading transport, corvée, salt and iron, coinage, granary intake and disbursement, and postal affairs across Henan, Shannan, Jiangxi, Huainan, and related circuits.

sentences.zh: 乾元二年，以本官加同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qianyuan, on the basis of his present office he was additionally made Associate Grand Councilor of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianyuan year 2 he was additionally made associate grand councilor while retaining his existing posts.

sentences.zh: 初，琦以國用未足，幣重貨輕，乃請鑄乾元重寶錢，以一當十行用之。

translations.literal: Earlier, because state expenditures were insufficient and currency was heavy while goods were light, Qi requested casting Qianyuan heavy treasure coins to circulate at one for ten.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, with state funds short and money overvalued relative to goods, he proposed casting Qianyuan heavy treasure coins valued at ten to one.

sentences.zh: 及作相，又請更鑄重輪乾元錢，一當五十，與乾元錢及開元通寶錢三品並行。

translations.literal: When he became chancellor he again requested casting heavy-rim Qianyuan coins at one for fifty, circulating together with Qianyuan coins and Kaiyuan universal treasure coins as three denominations.
translations.idiomatic: As chancellor he further proposed heavy-rim Qianyuan coins at fifty to one, circulating alongside standard Qianyuan and Kaiyuan coins as three denominations.

sentences.zh: 既而谷價騰貴，餓殣死亡，枕藉道路，又盜鑄爭起，中外皆以琦變法之弊，封奏日聞。

translations.literal: Before long grain prices soared; the starved and dead lay piled along the roads; counterfeiting and illicit casting rose in contention; within and without all attributed it to the harm of Qi's monetary reform, and sealed memorials were heard daily.
translations.idiomatic: Soon grain prices soared, the starving dead lined the roads, counterfeiting spread, and court and country alike blamed Qi's currency reform—memorials of protest arrived daily.

sentences.zh: 乾元二年十月，貶忠州長史，既在道，有告琦受人黃金二百兩者，遣御史劉期光追按之。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the second year of Qianyuan he was demoted to senior administrator of Zhong Prefecture; already on the road, someone reported that Qi had received two hundred taels of gold; Investigating Censor Liu Qiguang was sent to pursue and examine him.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of Qianyuan year 2 he was demoted to senior administrator of Zhong; on the road a report accused him of taking two hundred taels of gold, and Investigating Censor Liu Qiguang was sent to investigate.

sentences.zh: 琦對曰：二百兩金十三斤重，忝為宰相，不可自持。

translations.literal: Qi replied: 'Two hundred taels of gold weigh thirteen jin; I am humbly a chancellor and could not keep such a thing for myself.'
translations.idiomatic: Qi replied: 'Two hundred taels weigh thirteen jin; as a chancellor I could hardly keep such a sum for myself.'

sentences.zh: 若其付受有憑，即請準法科罪。

translations.literal: If there is proof of payment and receipt, then I ask to be punished according to law.'
translations.idiomatic: If there is proof of receipt, I ask to be punished by law.'

sentences.zh: 」期光以為此是琦伏罪也，遽奏之，請除名，配流夷州，馳驛發遣，仍差綱領送至彼。

translations.literal: ' Qiguang took this as Qi's confession of guilt, hastily memorialized, requested removal of his name from registers, and assignment to exile in Yi Prefecture; he was dispatched by urgent relay, and escort officers were also sent to deliver him there.
translations.idiomatic: Qiguang treated this as a confession, memorialized at once for expulsion and exile to Yi, dispatched him by urgent relay, and sent escorts to deliver him.

sentences.zh: 寶應初，起為朗州刺史，甚有能政，入遷太子賓客。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Baoying he was recalled as prefect of Lang Prefecture, with very able administration, and entered the capital as Mentor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Baoying he was recalled as prefect of Lang, governed with notable ability, and was then made mentor to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 屬吐蕃寇陷京師，代宗幸陜，關內副元帥郭子儀請琦為糧料使、兼御史大夫，充關內元帥副使。

translations.literal: When Tibetans raided and took the capital, Daizong went to Shaan; Guo Ziyi, deputy commander-in-chief of Guannei, requested Qi as grain commissioner and concurrent Censor-in-Chief, serving as deputy to the Guannei commander.
translations.idiomatic: When Tibetans seized the capital and Daizong fled to Shaan, Guo Ziyi, deputy commander of Guannei, asked for Qi as grain commissioner and concurrent censor-in-chief as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 未幾，改京兆尹。

translations.literal: Before long he was changed to Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made metropolitan governor of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 車駕克復，專判度支，兼諸道鑄錢鹽鐵轉運常平等使。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage recovered the capital, he had sole charge over revenue affairs and concurrently headed the commissioners for coinage, salt and iron, transport, and price stabilization in the various circuits.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor's return he again had sole charge of revenue and headed coinage, salt and iron, transport, and price-stabilization commissions across the circuits.

sentences.zh: 累封扶風郡公。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly enfeoffed as Duke of Fufeng Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as duke of Fufeng.

sentences.zh: 又加京兆尹，改戶部侍郎，判度支。

translations.literal: He was again made Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao, transferred to Vice Minister of Revenue, and given charge over revenue affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made metropolitan governor of Jingzhao, then vice minister of revenue with charge of revenue affairs.

sentences.zh: 前後領財賦十余年。

translations.literal: Before and after, he headed finance and tax affairs for more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: In all he directed state finance for more than ten years.

sentences.zh: 魚朝恩伏誅，琦坐與款狎，出為處州刺史，歷饒、湖二州。

translations.literal: When Yu Chao'en was executed, Qi was implicated for intimate familiarity with him and sent out as prefect of Chu Prefecture, passing through Rao and Hu prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu Chao'en was executed, Qi was punished for close ties with him and sent out as prefect of Chu, then Rao and Hu.

sentences.zh: 入為太子賓客、東都留司。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Mentor to the Heir Apparent and Eastern Capital retention officer.
translations.idiomatic: He returned as mentor to the heir apparent and retention officer at the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 上以其材，將復任用，召還京師，信宿而卒，年七十，贈太子少保。

translations.literal: The emperor, because of his talent, was about to employ him again and summoned him back to the capital; after one night's lodging he died, aged seventy, and was posthumously given the title of Junior Mentor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, valuing his talent, was about to reuse him and recalled him to the capital; he died after a single night's stay, aged seventy, and was posthumously made junior mentor to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 子峰，峰婦鄭氏女，皆以孝著，旌表其門。

translations.literal: His son Feng, and Feng's wife, a daughter of the Zheng clan, were all noted for filial piety; their gate was marked with commendation.
translations.idiomatic: His son Feng and Feng's wife, a daughter of the Zheng clan, were famed for filial piety; their household was officially commended.

sentences.zh: 班宏，衛州汲人也。

translations.literal: Ban Hong was a man of Ji in Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ban Hong came from Ji in Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 祖思簡，春官員外郎。

translations.literal: His grandfather Sijian was an Outside Officer of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Sijian was an outside officer of the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 父景倩，秘書監。

translations.literal: His father Jingqian was Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jingqian was director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 宏少舉進士，授右司禦胄曹，後為薛景先鳳翔掌書記，又為高適劍南觀察判官，累拜大理司直，攝監察御史。

translations.literal: Hong in youth passed the jinshi examination and was appointed to the Right Bureau of Imperial Carriages Armorers Office; later he was secretary to Xue Jingxian at Fengxiang, then administrative aide to Gao Shi as Jiannan observation commissioner; he was repeatedly promoted to Directing Rectifier of the Court of Judicial Review and acted as Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Hong passed the jinshi examination in youth and served in the imperial carriage bureau; he later was secretary to Xue Jingxian at Fengxiang and administrative aide to Gao Shi in Jiannan, then rose to directing rectifier of the judicial review court and acting investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 時青城山有妖賊張安居以左道惑眾，事覺，多誣引大將，冀以緩死，宏驗理而速殺之，人心乃安。

translations.literal: At the time on Mount Qingcheng the demonic bandit Zhang Anju used heterodox ways to delude the masses; when the matter was exposed he falsely implicated many great generals, hoping to delay death; Hong verified the facts and swiftly executed him, and popular sentiment was then settled.
translations.idiomatic: A sorcerer-rebel named Zhang Anju on Mount Qingcheng had misled the people with heterodox practices; when exposed he falsely implicated many generals to delay execution. Hong verified the case and executed him swiftly, restoring public calm.

sentences.zh: 既而郭英乂代適，以厭人望，奏署秘書郎，兼雒令，以疾免。

translations.literal: Before long Guo Yingyi replaced Shi; to satisfy public expectation he memorialized appointing Hong as Secretary and concurrent magistrate of Luo, but Hong was excused because of illness.
translations.idiomatic: When Guo Yingyi replaced Gao Shi, he appointed Hong secretary and concurrent magistrate of Luo to satisfy public expectation, but Hong resigned on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 大歷三年，遷起居舍人，尋兼理匭使，四遷至給事中。

translations.literal: In the third year of Dali he was transferred to Diarist of the Heir Apparent, soon after additionally charged with the complaint box, and through four promotions reached Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: In Dali year 3 he became diarist of the heir apparent, soon also oversaw the complaint box, and after four promotions reached supervising censor.

sentences.zh: 時李寶臣卒於其位，子惟嶽匿喪求位，上遣宏使成德問疾，且喻之。

translations.literal: At the time Li Baochen died in office; his son Wei Yue concealed the death and sought the post; the emperor sent Hong as envoy to Chengde to inquire after his health and also instruct him.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Baochen died in office his son Wei Yue concealed the death to seize the post; the emperor sent Hong to Chengde to inquire after his health and deliver instructions.

sentences.zh: 惟嶽厚賂宏，皆不受，還報合旨，遷刑部侍郎，兼京官考使。

translations.literal: Wei Yue richly bribed Hong, but he accepted none; on return his report accorded with the imperial intent; he was transferred to Vice Minister of Justice and concurrent examiner of capital officials.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yue offered rich bribes, which Hong refused; his report pleased the throne, and he was made vice minister of justice and examiner of capital officials.

sentences.zh: 時右僕射崔寧考兵部侍郎劉乃上下，宏駁曰：「夷荒靖難，專在節制，尺籍伍符，不校省司。

translations.literal: At the time Right Vice Director Cui Ning rated Vice Minister of War Liu Nai as lower-grade; Hong rebutted, saying: 'Pacifying the barbarian frontier lies solely with the military commissioners; rosters and tallies are not checked by the central ministries.'
translations.idiomatic: When Right Vice Director Cui Ning rated Vice Minister of War Liu Nai below standard, Hong objected: 'Frontier pacification rests with the military commissioners; troop rosters are not reviewed by the central ministries.'

sentences.zh: 夫上行宣美之名，則下開趨競之路；

translations.literal: When superiors proclaim names of beauty, then inferiors open paths of rivalry for favor;
translations.idiomatic: When superiors hand out praise too freely, subordinates open paths of rivalry;

sentences.zh: 上行阿容，下必朋黨。

translations.literal: when superiors show indulgent favor, inferiors will surely form cliques.'
translations.idiomatic: when superiors show indulgence, subordinates will surely form factions.'

sentences.zh: 」因削去之。

translations.literal: ' He therefore struck it out.
translations.idiomatic: He struck the rating out.

sentences.zh: 乃知而謝曰：「乃雖不敏，敢掠一美以僥二罪乎？

translations.literal: Nai learned of it and apologized, saying: 'Though Nai is not clever, how dare I seize one merit to escape two faults?'
translations.idiomatic: Liu Nai learned of it and apologized: 'Though I am no genius, how dare I claim one merit to escape two faults?'

sentences.zh: 」尋除吏部侍郎，為汪蕃會盟使李揆之副。

translations.literal: ' Soon after he was appointed Vice Minister of Civil Appointments and deputy to Li Kui, envoy for the Tang-Tibetan alliance.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made vice minister of civil appointments and deputy to Li Kui, envoy for the Tang-Tibetan alliance.

sentences.zh: 貞元初，仍歲旱蝗，上以賦調為急，改戶部侍郎，為度支使韓滉之副。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenyuan, with drought and locusts year after year, the emperor took tax levies as urgent; Hong was transferred to Vice Minister of Revenue and made deputy to the revenue commissioner Han Huang.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhenyuan, with drought and locusts year after year, the emperor made tax collection urgent; Hong became vice minister of revenue and deputy to revenue commissioner Han Huang.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書，復副竇參。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister and again served as deputy to Dou Can.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to minister and again served as deputy to Dou Can.

sentences.zh: 參初為大理司直，宏已為刑部侍郎，及參為相，領度支，上以宏久司國計，因令副之。

translations.literal: Can had early been Directing Rectifier of the Court of Judicial Review when Hong was already Vice Minister of Justice; when Can became chancellor and headed revenue affairs, because Hong had long managed state accounts the emperor therefore ordered him as deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Can had once been a judicial rectifier when Hong was already vice minister of justice; when Can became chancellor and headed revenue, the emperor made Hong his deputy because Hong had long managed state accounts.

sentences.zh: 且曰：「朕藉參宰相以臨遠，眾務悉委於卿，勿以辭也。

translations.literal: He also said: 'I rely on Chancellor Can to oversee distant matters; all affairs I entirely entrust to you—do not decline.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: 'I rely on Chancellor Can for distant affairs; I entrust all business to you—do not refuse.'

sentences.zh: 」參以先貴，常私解悅之曰：「參後來，一朝居尚書之上，甚不自安，一年之後，當歸此使。

translations.literal: ' Because Can had earlier been senior in rank, he often privately soothed him, saying: 'Can came later; to sit one morning above the Minister is very unsettling to me—in a year's time I shall return this commissioner post.'
translations.idiomatic: Can, who had once outranked him, often reassured him privately: 'I came later; sitting above you as minister unsettles me—in a year I shall return the revenue post to you.'

sentences.zh: 」宏心喜，歲餘，參絕不復言。

translations.literal: ' Hong was pleased in heart; after more than a year Can never spoke of it again.
translations.idiomatic: Hong was delighted, but after more than a year Can never mentioned it again.

sentences.zh: 宏性剛愎，為人間之，且怒食言，公事多異。

translations.literal: Hong's nature was stubborn and obstinate; someone informed on this to him, and he was angry at the broken promise; public business often diverged.
translations.idiomatic: Hong was stubborn by nature; when someone told him of Can's promise he grew angry at the broken word, and their official dealings often clashed.

sentences.zh: 揚子院，鹽鐵轉運委藏也，宏以御史中丞徐粲主之，既不理，且以賄聞，參欲代之，宏執不可。

translations.literal: The Yangzi depot was the entrusted storehouse of salt-and-iron transport; Hong had Vice Censor-in-Chief Xu Can head it—he neither managed it properly and bribery was reported; Can wished to replace him, but Hong insisted it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: The Yangzi depot was the salt-and-iron transport storehouse, which Hong placed under Vice Censor-in-Chief Xu Can; Xu neglected his duties and bribery was reported. Can wanted to replace him, but Hong refused.

sentences.zh: 參又選諸院吏，未嘗訪宏，乃疏參所用者過惡以聞，事輒留中。

translations.literal: Can again selected depot clerks without ever consulting Hong; Hong then memorialized the faults and crimes of those Can employed, and matters were always held within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Can selected depot clerks without consulting Hong; Hong memorialized their faults and the emperor withheld approval.

sentences.zh: 無何，參以使勞加吏部尚書，而宏進封蕭國公，怨參以虛號寵之，間惡愈甚。

translations.literal: Before long Can, for mission labor, was additionally made Minister of Civil Appointments, while Hong was advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of Xiao; Hong resented that Can used an empty title to favor him, and secret hostility grew worse.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Can was made minister of civil appointments for his mission work while Hong was enfeoffed duke of Xiao; Hong resented the empty honor and their secret enmity deepened.

sentences.zh: 每奉詔營建，宏必極壯麗，親程課役，又厚結權幸以傾參。

translations.literal: Whenever he received edicts for construction, Hong always made them extremely magnificent, personally measuring out corvée labor, and also richly cultivated favorites to overthrow Can.
translations.idiomatic: On every construction edict Hong built on a lavish scale, personally supervised labor, and cultivated powerful favorites to undermine Can.

sentences.zh: 張滂先善於宏，宏薦為司農少卿，及參欲以滂分掌江淮鹽鐵，詢之於宏，宏以滂嫉惡，慮以法繩徐粲，因曰：「滂強戾難制，不可用。

translations.literal: Zhang Pang had earlier been on good terms with Hong; Hong recommended him as Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Granary; when Can wished to have Pang share charge of Jiang-Huai salt and iron, he inquired of Hong; Hong, because Pang was jealous and harsh, feared he would use the law to bind Xu Can, and therefore said: 'Pang is forceful, perverse, and hard to control—he cannot be used.'
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Pang had been friendly with Hong, who recommended him as vice director of the imperial granary court. When Can wanted Pang to share Jiang-Huai salt and iron, he asked Hong, who feared Pang's harsh nature would prosecute Xu Can and said: 'Pang is violent and ungovernable—he cannot be used.'

sentences.zh: 」滂知之。

translations.literal: ' Pang learned of it.
translations.idiomatic: Pang learned of this.

sentences.zh: 八年三月，參遂為上所疏，乃讓度支使，遂以宏專判，而參不欲使務悉歸於宏，問計京兆尹薛玨，玨曰：「二子交惡，而滂剛決，若分鹽鐵轉運於滂，必能制宏。

translations.literal: In the third month of the eighth year Can was finally impeached by the emperor, relinquished the revenue commissioner post, and Hong was given sole charge; but Can did not wish all commissioner affairs to return wholly to Hong and asked advice of Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao Xue Jue; Jue said: 'The two men are mutually hostile, and Pang is firm and decisive—if salt-and-iron transport is divided to Pang, he will surely be able to control Hong.'
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of year 8 Can was impeached, gave up the revenue post, and Hong took sole charge. Unwilling to let Hong control everything, Can asked Metropolitan Governor Xue Jue, who said: 'They hate each other; Pang is resolute—give him salt and transport and he can check Hong.'

sentences.zh: 」參乃薦滂為戶部侍郎、鹽鐵使、判轉運，尚隸於宏以悅之。

translations.literal: ' Can then recommended Pang as Vice Minister of Revenue, salt-and-iron commissioner, and with charge over transport, still subordinate to Hong to please him.
translations.idiomatic: Can then recommended Pang as vice minister of revenue, salt commissioner, and transport chief, nominally still under Hong to placate him.

sentences.zh: 江淮兩稅，悉宏主之，置巡院，然令宏、滂共擇其官。

translations.literal: The two taxes of Jiang-Huai were entirely headed by Hong; inspection depots were established, yet Hong and Pang were ordered jointly to choose their officials.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang-Huai's two taxes remained under Hong, with inspection depots established, but Hong and Pang were to choose officials jointly.

sentences.zh: 滂請鹽鐵舊簿書於宏，宏不與之。

translations.literal: Pang requested the old salt-and-iron account books from Hong; Hong would not give them.
translations.idiomatic: Pang asked Hong for the old salt-and-iron ledgers; Hong refused.

sentences.zh: 每署院官，宏、滂更相是非，莫有用者。

translations.literal: Whenever depot officials were appointed, Hong and Pang each criticized the other; none could be used.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever depot officials were appointed, Hong and Pang vetoed each other's choices until none could serve.

sentences.zh: 滂乃奏曰：「班宏與臣相戾，巡院多闕官。

translations.literal: Pang then memorialized: 'Ban Hong and your servant are at odds; the inspection depots have many vacant posts.'
translations.idiomatic: Pang memorialized: 'Ban Hong and I are at odds; the inspection depots have many vacancies.'

sentences.zh: 臣掌財賦，國家大計，職不修，無所逃罪。

translations.literal: Your servant heads finance and tax affairs, the great plan of the state; if duties are not fulfilled, there is no escaping guilt.
translations.idiomatic: I head state finance—a great charge; if I cannot perform my duties, I cannot escape blame.

sentences.zh: 今宏若此，何以輯事？

translations.literal: Now if Hong is like this, how can affairs be brought together?'
translations.idiomatic: With Hong acting thus, how can affairs be managed?'

sentences.zh: 」遂令分掌之。

translations.literal: ' The order was then given to divide and share charge of them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered a division of responsibilities.

sentences.zh: 無幾，宏言於宰相趙憬、陸贄曰：「宏職轉運，年運江淮米五十萬斛，前年增七十萬斛，以實太倉，幸無過。

translations.literal: Before long Hong spoke to the chancellors Zhao Jing and Lu Zhi, saying: 'In Hong's transport duties, each year five hundred thousand hu of Jiang-Huai rice are transported; the year before last it increased to seven hundred thousand hu to fill the Grand Granary—fortunately without fault.'
translations.idiomatic: Soon Hong told Chancellors Zhao Jing and Lu Zhi: 'In my transport duties I move five hundred thousand hu of Jiang-Huai grain yearly; two years ago I raised it to seven hundred thousand to fill the Grand Granary—and have done no wrong.'

sentences.zh: 今職移於人，不知何謂？

translations.literal: Now the post has shifted to another—what is this to mean?'
translations.idiomatic: Now the post has passed to another—what does that mean?'

sentences.zh: 」滂時在側，忿然曰：「尚書失言甚矣！

translations.literal: ' Pang was then at his side and said angrily: 'Minister, you have spoken very wrongly!'
translations.idiomatic: Pang, who was present, said angrily: 'Minister, you speak very wrongly!'

sentences.zh: 若運務畢舉，朝廷固不奪之，蓋由喪公錢、縱奸吏故也。

translations.literal: If transport duties were fully accomplished, the court would certainly not take them away—it is because public funds were lost and corrupt clerks were indulged.
translations.idiomatic: If transport were well managed the court would not have removed you—it was because public funds were lost and corrupt clerks indulged.

sentences.zh: 且凡為度支胥吏，不一歲，資累鉅萬，僮馬第宅，僭於王公，非盜官財何以致是？

translations.literal: Moreover, all who become revenue clerks, within less than a year, accumulate assets of tens of thousands; servants, horses, mansions rival kings and dukes—if not by stealing official wealth, how could they reach this?'
translations.idiomatic: Every revenue clerk within a year amasses tens of thousands in wealth, with servants, horses, and mansions rivaling princes—how else but by stealing public funds?'

sentences.zh: 道呼喧喧，無不知之，聖上故令滂分掌。

translations.literal: The roads resound with clamor—none do not know it; the sage sovereign therefore ordered Pang to share charge.
translations.idiomatic: The whole road rings with talk of it; that is why the emperor ordered me to share charge.

sentences.zh: 公向所言，無乃歸怨於上乎、」宏默然不對。

translations.literal: What you just said—are you not shifting blame onto the sovereign?' Hong was silent and did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: What you just said—are you not shifting blame onto the emperor?' Hong fell silent.

sentences.zh: 是日，宏稱疾於第，滂往問之，宏不見，憬、贄乃以宏、滂之言上聞。

translations.literal: That day Hong claimed illness at his residence; Pang went to inquire after him, but Hong would not see him; Jing and Zhi then reported Hong's and Pang's words to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: That day Hong claimed illness at home; Pang called on him but was refused audience; Zhao Jing and Lu Zhi reported their exchange to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 由是遵大歷故事，如劉晏、韓滉所分。

translations.literal: Thereby they followed the Dali precedent, as Liu Yan and Han Huang had divided it.
translations.idiomatic: They then followed the Dali precedent, as Liu Yan and Han Huang had divided responsibilities.

sentences.zh: 滂至揚州按徐粲，逮仆妾子侄，得贓鉅萬，乃徙嶺表。

translations.literal: Pang went to Yangzhou to investigate Xu Can, arrested servants, concubines, sons, and nephews, obtained bribes of tens of thousands, and then banished him to the Lingnan region.
translations.idiomatic: Pang went to Yangzhou to investigate Xu Can, arrested his household, uncovered tens of thousands in bribes, and exiled him to the far south.

sentences.zh: 故參得罪，宏頗有力焉。

translations.literal: Therefore when Can fell from grace, Hong had considerable force in it.
translations.idiomatic: Thus when Can fell, Hong had played a major part.

sentences.zh: 勤恪官署，晨入夕歸，下吏勞而未嘗厭苦，清白勤幹，稱之於時。

translations.literal: Diligent and respectful in office, entering at dawn and returning at dusk, subordinate clerks labored yet he never showed weariness or suffering; upright, diligent, and capable—he was praised in his time.
translations.idiomatic: He was diligent in office, arriving at dawn and leaving at dusk; though his clerks toiled he never complained. Upright and capable, he was praised in his day.

sentences.zh: 貞元八年七月卒，年七十三，廢朝，加贈，謚曰敬。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the eighth year of Zhenyuan he died, aged seventy-three; court was suspended; additional posthumous honors were given; his posthumous title was Respectful.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the seventh month of Zhenyuan year 8, aged seventy-three; court mourning was ordered, posthumous honors were granted, and he was given the posthumous title Respectful.

sentences.zh: 王紹，本家於太原，今為京兆萬年人。

translations.literal: Wang Shao's family was originally from Taiyuan; he is now a man of Wannian in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shao's family came originally from Taiyuan; he was now registered in Wannian in the capital district.

sentences.zh: 舊名與憲宗同，永貞年改焉。

translations.literal: His former name was the same as Xianzong's; in the Yongzhen era it was changed.
translations.idiomatic: His original personal name matched Xianzong's and was changed in the Yongzhen era.

sentences.zh: 少時，顏真卿器重之，因紹舊名，字之曰德素，奏授武康尉。

translations.literal: In youth Yan Zhenqing greatly valued him; because of Shao's former name, he gave him the style Desu and memorialized appointing him as defender of Wukang.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Yan Zhenqing esteemed him, gave him the style name Desu because of his former name, and had him appointed defender of Wukang.

sentences.zh: 蕭復為常州刺史，辟為從事；

translations.literal: When Xiao Fu was prefect of Chang Prefecture, he recruited him as an aide;
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Fu was prefect of Chang, he recruited him as an aide;

sentences.zh: 包佶領租庸鹽鐵，亦以紹為判官。

translations.literal: when Bao Ji headed corvée, salt, and iron affairs, he also used Shao as administrative aide.
translations.idiomatic: when Bao Ji headed corvée, salt, and iron affairs, he also made Shao his administrative aide.

sentences.zh: 時李希烈阻兵，江淮租輸，所在艱阻，特移運路自潁入汴。

translations.literal: At the time Li Xilie blocked the armies; Jiang-Huai tax transport everywhere met hardship; the transport route was specially shifted from Ying into Bian.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Xilie blocked the roads, Jiang-Huai tax shipments faced hardship everywhere, and the transport route was rerouted from Ying into the Bian Canal.

sentences.zh: 紹奉佶表詣闕，屬德宗西幸，紹乃督緣路輕貨，趣金、商路，倍程出洋州以赴行在。

translations.literal: Shao, carrying Ji's memorial to court, found Dezong had gone west on campaign; Shao then supervised light goods along the route, hastening by the Jin and Shang roads, doubling the journey to leave Yang Prefecture and reach the mobile court.
translations.idiomatic: Shao carried Ji's memorial to court just as Dezong fled west; he supervised light goods along the route, took the Jin and Shang roads at double speed, and left Yang Prefecture to reach the mobile court.

sentences.zh: 德宗親勞之，謂紹曰：「六軍未有春服，我猶衣裘。

translations.literal: Dezong personally comforted him and said to Shao: 'The Six Armies have no spring clothing; I still wear fur.'
translations.idiomatic: Dezong personally received him and said: 'The Six Armies lack spring clothing; I still wear furs.'

sentences.zh: 」紹俯伏流涕，奏曰：「包佶令臣間道進奉數約五十萬。

translations.literal: ' Shao prostrated himself with tears and memorialized: 'Bao Ji ordered your servant by secret route to present tribute of about five hundred thousand.'
translations.idiomatic: Shao prostrated himself in tears and reported: 'Bao Ji sent me by secret route with tribute of roughly five hundred thousand.'
