sentences.zh: 」上曰：道路回遠，經費懸急，卿之所奏，豈可望耶？

translations.literal: ' The emperor said: 'The roads wind far; expenses hang in urgent need—what you report, how can it be hoped for?'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: 'The roads are long and funds desperately short—how can I expect what you report?'

sentences.zh: 」後五日而所督繼至，上深賴焉。

translations.literal: ' Five days later what he had supervised arrived in succession; the emperor deeply relied on this.
translations.idiomatic: Five days later the goods he had supervised arrived, and the emperor relied on him deeply.

sentences.zh: 貞元中，為倉部員外郎。

translations.literal: During Zhenyuan he was Outside Officer of the Bureau of Granaries.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenyuan era he became an outside officer of the Bureau of Granaries.

sentences.zh: 時屬兵革旱蝗之後，令戶部收闕官俸，兼稅茶及諸色無名之錢，以為水旱之備。

translations.literal: The time fell after warfare, drought, and locusts; the Revenue Ministry was ordered to collect vacant official salaries, and additionally tax tea and various unnamed levies as preparation against flood and drought.
translations.idiomatic: After war, drought, and locusts the Revenue Ministry was ordered to collect vacant official salaries and tax tea and various unnamed levies as reserves against flood and drought.

sentences.zh: 紹自拜倉部，便準詔主判，及遷戶部、兵部郎中，皆獨司其務。

translations.literal: From the time Shao took the granary post he followed the edict as chief judge; when transferred to Director in the Revenue and War ministries, he alone managed those duties.
translations.idiomatic: From his granary appointment Shao acted under edict as chief administrator, and when promoted to director in the revenue and war ministries he alone managed those duties.

sentences.zh: 擢拜戶部侍郎，尋判度支。

translations.literal: He was promoted and appointed Vice Minister of Revenue, soon given charge over revenue affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice minister of revenue and soon given charge of revenue affairs.

sentences.zh: 後二年，遷戶部尚書。

translations.literal: Two years later he was transferred to Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later he was made minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 德宗臨馭歲久，機務不由臺司，自竇參、陸贄已後，宰臣備位而已。

translations.literal: Dezong had held the throne many years; key affairs did not pass through the Secretariat; since Dou Can and Lu Zhi, grand councilors merely filled posts.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong had reigned many years; key affairs no longer ran through the secretariat, and since Dou Can and Lu Zhi the grand councilors had been figureheads.

sentences.zh: 德宗以紹謹密，恩遇特異，凡主重務八年，政之大小，多所訪決。

translations.literal: Dezong, because Shao was careful and discreet, treated him with special favor; for eight years in all he headed weighty duties, and affairs great and small were largely referred to him for decision.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong favored Shao for his discretion; for eight years he held key posts and the emperor consulted him on matters large and small.

sentences.zh: 紹未賞泄漏，亦不矜衒。

translations.literal: Shao never rewarded leaks, nor did he show off.
translations.idiomatic: He neither rewarded leaks nor boasted of his influence.

sentences.zh: 順宗即位，王叔文始奪其權，拜兵部尚書，尋除檢校吏部尚書、東都留守。

translations.literal: When Shunzong took the throne, Wang Shuwen first stripped his power; he was appointed Minister of War, soon removed as Acting Minister of Civil Appointments and Eastern Capital retention officer.
translations.idiomatic: When Shunzong came to the throne Wang Shuwen stripped his power; he was made minister of war, then acting minister of civil appointments and retention officer at the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 元和初，遷檢校尚書右僕射、徐州刺史、武寧軍節度，復以濠、泗二州隸焉。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanhe he was transferred to Acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, prefect of Xuzhou, and military commissioner of Wuning; Hao and Si prefectures were again placed under him.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yuanhe he became acting right vice director, prefect of Xuzhou, and Wuning military commissioner, with Hao and Si again under his command.

sentences.zh: 時承張愔之後，兵驕難治，紹修輯軍政，人甚安之。

translations.literal: The time followed Zhang Yin; the armies were arrogant and hard to govern; Shao repaired and ordered military administration, and the people were greatly settled.
translations.idiomatic: Following Zhang Yin, the armies were arrogant and hard to control; Shao restored military discipline and the people were greatly reassured.

sentences.zh: 六年，征拜兵部尚書，兼判戶部事。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was summoned and appointed Minister of War, with concurrent charge over Revenue Ministry affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In year 6 he was recalled as minister of war with concurrent charge of revenue affairs.

sentences.zh: 九年卒，年七十二，贈左僕射，謚曰敬。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he died, aged seventy-two; he was posthumously given Left Vice Director and the posthumous title Respectful.
translations.idiomatic: He died in year 9, aged seventy-two, and was posthumously made left vice director with the posthumous title Respectful.

sentences.zh: 李巽，字令叔，趙郡人。

translations.literal: Li Xun, styled Lingshu, was a man of Zhao Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xun, whose style name was Lingshu, came from Zhao Commandery.

sentences.zh: 少苦心為學，以明經調補華州參軍，拔萃登科，授鄠縣尉。

translations.literal: In youth he labored at learning; through the Mingjing examination he was transferred to military aide of Hua Prefecture; by special selection he passed the examination and was appointed defender of E County.
translations.idiomatic: He studied hard in youth, passed the Mingjing examination and became a military aide in Hua Prefecture, then by special selection gained office and was made defender of E County.

sentences.zh: 周歷臺省，由左司郎中出為常州刺史。

translations.literal: He passed through the central ministries; from Director of the Left Bureau he went out as prefect of Chang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He served throughout the central ministries and left as director of the left bureau to become prefect of Chang.

sentences.zh: 逾年，召為給事中，出為湖南觀察使，銳於為理。

translations.literal: After a year he was recalled as Supervising Censor and sent out as Hunan observation commissioner, sharp in governance.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was recalled as supervising censor and sent out as Hunan observation commissioner, governing with sharp rigor.

sentences.zh: 五年，改江西觀察使，加檢校散騎常侍、兼御史大夫。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was changed to Jiangxi observation commissioner, additionally made Acting Regular Attendant and concurrent Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 he became Jiangxi observation commissioner and was additionally made acting regular attendant and concurrent censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 巽持下以法，吏不敢欺，而動必察之。

translations.literal: Xun held subordinates by law; clerks did not dare deceive him, and every movement he surely examined.
translations.idiomatic: Xun governed subordinates by law; clerks dared not deceive him, and he scrutinized every action.

sentences.zh: 順宗即位，入為兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: When Shunzong took the throne, he entered the capital as Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: When Shunzong came to the throne he entered the capital as vice minister of war.

sentences.zh: 司徒杜佑判度支鹽鐵轉運使，以巽幹治，奏為副使。

translations.literal: Situ Du You had charge over revenue, salt and iron, and transport commissioners; because Xun was capable in administration, he memorialized him as deputy commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Situ Du You headed revenue, salt and iron, and transport; he recommended Xun as deputy commissioner for his administrative skill.

sentences.zh: 佑辭重位，巽遂專領度支鹽鐵使。

translations.literal: You declined the heavy post; Xun then solely headed the revenue and salt-and-iron commissioner posts.
translations.idiomatic: When You stepped down, Xun took sole charge of revenue and salt and iron.

sentences.zh: 榷筦之法，號為難重，唯大歷中僕射劉晏雅得其術，賦入豐羨。

translations.literal: The monopoly control law was called difficult and weighty; only in Dali did Vice Director Liu Yan elegantly grasp its method, and tax intake was abundant and overflowing.
translations.idiomatic: Monopoly administration was considered the hardest fiscal task; only Liu Yan in the Dali era had mastered it and filled the treasury.

sentences.zh: 巽掌使一年，征課所入，類晏之多歲，明年過之，又一年加一百八十萬貫。

translations.literal: In one year of Xun heading the commission, levies collected matched Yan's best years; the next year exceeded it; in another year it increased by 1.8 million strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: In his first year as commissioner revenue matched Yan's best years; the next year surpassed it; in the third year it rose by 1.8 million strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 舊制，每歲運江淮米五十萬斛抵河陰，久不盈其數，唯巽三年登焉。

translations.literal: By old regulation each year five hundred thousand hu of Jiang-Huai rice were transported to Heyin; for long the quota was not filled—only under Xun in three years was it reached.
translations.idiomatic: By regulation five hundred thousand hu of Jiang-Huai grain were shipped yearly to Heyin; for years the quota was missed—only Xun met it within three years.

sentences.zh: 遷兵部尚書，明年改吏部尚書，使任如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of War; the next year changed to Minister of Civil Appointments, with commissioner duties as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was made minister of war, then minister of civil appointments the next year, retaining his commissioner duties.

sentences.zh: 巽精於吏職，蓋性使然也。

translations.literal: Xun was expert in clerical duties—this was surely his nature.
translations.idiomatic: Xun excelled at administrative work by nature.

sentences.zh: 雖在私家，亦置案牘簿書，勾檢如公署焉。

translations.literal: Even in private life he set out documents and ledgers, checking and examining as in a public office.
translations.idiomatic: Even at home he kept documents and ledgers and audited them as in a government office.

sentences.zh: 人吏有過，絲毫無所貸，雖在千里外，其恐栗如在巽前。

translations.literal: When subordinate clerks had faults, not a hair's breadth was forgiven; though a thousand li away, their fear and trembling were as if before Xun.
translations.idiomatic: He forgave no fault in subordinates; clerks a thousand li away trembled as if before him.

sentences.zh: 初，程異附王叔文貶竄，巽知其吏才明辯，奏而用之，憲宗不違其請。

translations.literal: Earlier, Cheng Yi had attached to Wang Shuwen and was banished; Xun knew his clerical talent was bright and argumentative, memorialized and used him, and Xianzong did not oppose the request.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Yi, banished for ties to Wang Shuwen, was known to Xun for sharp administrative talent; Xun memorialized to employ him and Xianzong agreed.

sentences.zh: 異勾檢簿籍，又精於巽，故課最加衍，亦異之助焉。

translations.literal: Yi checked ledgers and was even more expert than Xun; therefore annual assessments increased and expanded—this too was Yi's assistance.
translations.idiomatic: Yi audited the books with even greater skill than Xun, so revenue targets rose year by year—with Yi's help.

sentences.zh: 巽為吏部尚書，臥疾，郎官相率省問，巽初不言其病，與之考校程課，商略功利，至其夕而卒。

translations.literal: Xun as Minister of Civil Appointments lay ill; bureau officials came in succession to inquire; Xun at first did not speak of his illness, but with them examined schedules and courses, discussed profit and utility—and by that evening he died.
translations.idiomatic: As minister of civil appointments Xun fell ill; when bureau officials called he did not mention his illness but reviewed schedules and discussed revenue with them—and died that evening.

sentences.zh: 然性強很狡惡，忌刻頗甚，乘德宗之怒，謀殺竇參，物論冤之。

translations.literal: Yet his nature was forceful, obstinate, crafty, and vicious, and jealous to a high degree; seizing Dezong's anger he plotted Dou Can's death—public opinion held it an injustice.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was stubborn, crafty, and deeply jealous; exploiting Dezong's anger he engineered Dou Can's death, which public opinion deemed unjust.

sentences.zh: 初，參為宰相，不悅於巽，自左司郎中出為常州刺史，仍促其行。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Can was chancellor he disliked Xun and sent him from Director of the Left Bureau out as prefect of Chang, still pressing him to depart quickly.
translations.idiomatic: When Can was chancellor he disliked Xun and sent him from the left bureau directorship to Chang prefecture, urging a quick departure.

sentences.zh: 不數月，參貶郴州司馬。

translations.literal: Within a few months Can was demoted to military adjutant of Chen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Within months Can was demoted to military adjutant of Chen.

sentences.zh: 久之，巽自給事中為湖南觀察使，郴即屬郡也。

translations.literal: After a long time Xun went from Supervising Censor to Hunan observation commissioner; Chen was precisely a subordinate commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward Xun became Hunan observation commissioner from supervising censor; Chen was under his jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 宣武軍節度使劉士寧以擅襲父任，物議不可，朝廷不得已而授之。

translations.literal: Xuanwu military commissioner Liu Shining, for seizing his father's post on his own authority, was unacceptable in public opinion; the court had no choice but to grant it.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanwu commissioner Liu Shining seized his father's post on his own authority, which public opinion rejected; the court granted it only reluctantly.

sentences.zh: 及參之貶，士寧嘗以絹數千匹賂參，巽在湖南具奏其事，言參與籓鎮交通，德宗怒，遂賜參死，議者冤之。

translations.literal: When Can was demoted, Shining had once bribed Can with several thousand bolts of silk; Xun in Hunan fully memorialized the matter, saying Can had dealings with military commissioners; Dezong was angry and then ordered Can's death—commentators held it an injustice.
translations.idiomatic: When Can was demoted, Shining had once bribed him with thousands of bolts of silk. Xun in Hunan reported that Can had dealings with regional commanders; Dezong in anger ordered Can's death, which many regarded as unjust.

sentences.zh: 巽廉察江西，徇喜怒之情，而無罪被戮者多矣。

translations.literal: Xun as inspector of Jiangxi followed moods of pleasure and anger; many without crime were executed.
translations.idiomatic: As Jiangxi inspector Xun indulged personal moods, and many innocent men were executed.

sentences.zh: 元和四年四月卒，時年七十一，贈尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the fourth year of Yuanhe he died, aged seventy-one, and was posthumously given Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth month of Yuanhe year 4, aged seventy-one, and was posthumously made left vice director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：歷代操利柄為國計者，莫不損下益上，危人自安，變法以弄權，斂怨以構禍，皆有之矣。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: In every age those who grasped the profit lever for state planning have without exception harmed those below to benefit those above, endangered others to secure themselves, changed laws to manipulate power, and gathered resentment to build calamity—all have had these.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: Throughout history those who held fiscal power for state planning have harmed the people to enrich the throne, endangered others for their own safety, changed laws to manipulate power, and gathered resentment unto disaster.

sentences.zh: 如劉晏通擁滯，任才能，富其國而不勞於民，儉於家而利於眾。

translations.literal: Such as Liu Yan, who understood hoarding and release, employed talent and ability, enriched his state without taxing the people, was frugal in his household yet benefited the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yan understood hoarding and release, employed talent wisely, enriched the state without burdening the people, and was frugal at home while benefiting the public.

sentences.zh: 或問曰：鄭子產吏不能欺，宓子賤吏不忍欺，西門豹吏不敢欺。

translations.literal: Someone asked: 'With Zichan of Zheng, clerks could not deceive him; with Master Mi Jian, clerks could not bear to deceive him; with Ximen Bao, clerks did not dare deceive him.'
translations.idiomatic: Someone asked: 'Zichan of Zheng—clerks could not deceive him; Master Mi Jian—clerks could not bear to deceive him; Ximen Bao—clerks dared not deceive him.'

sentences.zh: 三子者，古之賢人也，吏皆懷其欺而不能、不忍、不敢也。

translations.literal: These three men were worthy men of antiquity; clerks all harbored thoughts of deceit yet could not, could not bear to, or did not dare.
translations.idiomatic: These three were sages of antiquity; clerks might think to deceive them yet could not, could not bear to, or dared not.

sentences.zh: 晏之吏，遠近自不欺者何也？

translations.literal: Yan's clerks, near and far, were not deceived on their own—why?
translations.idiomatic: Why were Yan's clerks, near and far, not deceiving him of their own accord?

sentences.zh: 答曰：蓋任其才而得其人也。

translations.literal: The answer says: It was because he entrusted tasks to their talents and obtained the right men.
translations.idiomatic: The answer: he entrusted work to capable men and chose the right people.

sentences.zh: 晏歿，故吏二十余年繼掌財賦，不其是哉！

translations.literal: When Yan died, his former clerks for more than twenty years in succession held finance and tax affairs—is this not proof?
translations.idiomatic: After Yan's death his former clerks ran state finance for more than twenty years—is that not proof?

sentences.zh: 《史記貨殖》云：「平糶齊物，關市不乏，治國之道也。

translations.literal: The 'Treatise on Commodities' in the Records of the Grand Historian says: 'Equalizing grain sales and leveling goods, keeping markets and passes supplied—this is the way to govern a state.'
translations.idiomatic: The Treatise on Commodities in the Records says: 'Equalizing grain sales and leveling prices, keeping markets supplied—that is how to govern a state.'

sentences.zh: 」晏治天下，無甚貴甚賤之物，泛言治國者，其可及乎！

translations.literal: ' Yan governed the realm so there were no extremely dear or extremely cheap goods; those who speak broadly of governing a state—can they reach this!
translations.idiomatic: Yan governed the realm so that nothing became extremely dear or cheap—can those who speak generally of statecraft match him!

sentences.zh: 舉真卿才，忠也，減王縉罪，正也，忠正之道，復出於人，嗚呼！

translations.literal: Recommending Zhenqing's talent was loyalty; reducing Wang Jin's penalty was rectitude—the way of loyalty and rectitude reappeared in a man—alas!
translations.idiomatic: Recommending Zhenqing showed loyalty; lightening Wang Jin's sentence showed rectitude—the way of loyalty and justice lived again in a man—alas!

sentences.zh: 本秀於林，風必摧之，常袞見忌於前，楊炎致冤於後，可為長嘆息矣！

translations.literal: A tree outstanding in the forest—the wind surely breaks it; Chang Gao was jealous of him before, Yang Yan brought injustice after—one may sigh long over this!
translations.idiomatic: A tree that stands out in the forest is broken by the wind; Chang Gao envied him before, Yang Yan wronged him after—how deeply one must sigh!

sentences.zh: 時譏有口者以利啖之，茍不塞讒口，何以持重權？

translations.literal: The age mocked that those with mouths were fed with profit; if one did not stop slanderous mouths, how could one hold heavy power?
translations.idiomatic: The age mocked him for buying off critics; yet without silencing slander, how could he hold great power?

sentences.zh: 即無以展其才，濟其國矣。

translations.literal: Then he could not display his talent or rescue his state.
translations.idiomatic: Without that he could neither display his talent nor save the state.

sentences.zh: 是其術也，又何譏焉。

translations.literal: This was his method—why mock it further?
translations.idiomatic: That was his method—why mock it?

sentences.zh: 第五琦促辦應卒，民不加賦，而國豐饒，亦庶幾矣。

translations.literal: Di Wuqi pressed completion to meet emergencies; the people were not given added levies, yet the state was abundant—this too nearly succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Di Wuqi met emergencies swiftly without raising taxes, and the state grew rich—he nearly succeeded.

sentences.zh: 然鑄錢變法，物貴身危，其何陋哉！

translations.literal: Yet casting coin and changing law made goods dear and his person endangered—how base!
translations.idiomatic: Yet his coin reforms made goods dear and endangered his own life—how crude a policy!

sentences.zh: 凡利國者，農商之外，不可為也。

translations.literal: Whatever profits the state—apart from agriculture and commerce—must not be done.
translations.idiomatic: State profit must come only from agriculture and commerce, not elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 宏、滂爭權樹黨，皆非令人。

translations.literal: Hong and Pang fought for power and planted factions—neither was a man to admire.
translations.idiomatic: Hong and Pang fought for power and built factions—neither was admirable.

sentences.zh: 紹之謹密幹事，巽之皦察精辨，亦足可稱。

translations.literal: Shao's careful discretion in handling affairs, Xun's bright scrutiny and keen discrimination—both are also worthy of praise.
translations.idiomatic: Shao's discreet competence and Xun's sharp scrutiny are also praiseworthy.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：豐財忠良，晏道為長。

translations.literal: The encomium says: Enriching the treasury with loyal worth—Yan's way was foremost.
translations.idiomatic: Encomium: Enriching the treasury through loyal service—Yan's way stood foremost.

sentences.zh: 琦、宏、滂、巽，鹹以利彰。

translations.literal: Qi, Hong, Pang, and Xun—all were renowned through profit.
translations.idiomatic: Qi, Hong, Pang, and Xun—all won fame through fiscal skill.
